page: UpCloud CLOUDNATIVE-4xCPU-32GB is a memory-optimized virtual server instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features 4 shared vCPUs based on the x86_64 AMD EPYC 7542 processor running at 2.0 GHz. The hardware configuration includes 32.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU. This instance does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, but it comes with one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Performance benchmarks reflect its shared CPU allocation and moderate clock speed. The instance demonstrates average performance in single-core Geekbench and Passmark CPU tests, alongside average memory bandwidth for small cached blocks. However, multi-core execution is constrained, with stress-ng multi-core CPU performance and Geekbench multi-core scores falling into the weak category. Large-block memory bandwidth and Redis SET operations also show weak throughput, while static web serving and medium-model LLM inference speeds are poor.

Given its shared CPU model and high memory density, this instance offers a cost-efficient profile for memory-bound workloads that do not require sustained, high-performance CPU throughput. It is well-suited for caching layers, moderate database operations, text processing, and lightweight background workers. It is less suitable for CPU-intensive tasks, large-scale web serving, or complex machine learning inference due to its shared resource allocation and lower multi-core benchmark results.
